questions.q: Can a brand publish a campaign live without a funded escrow hold, bypassing the same gate PATCH-to-ACTIVE enforces?
questions.a: YES — CampaignService.create() never calls requireFundedEscrow(); only update() does. See CAMP-01.

questions.q: Is the brand publish fee charged when a campaign is created directly as ACTIVE instead of DRAFT-then-PATCH?
questions.a: NO — same root cause as above; brandCampaignFeeService.chargeOnPublish is only called from update() and ConfirmLaunchExecutor, never create().

questions.q: Do CampaignController, CreatorController, ExternalCreatorController, ReportExportController, CreatorApplicationController have controller-level tests?
questions.a: NO for all five (confirmed by exhaustive filename search of src/test/java/com/influora/web). CampaignTemplateController and CreatorCampaignController DO have controller tests, both run green in this session.

questions.q: Is the CAMPAIGN_TEMPLATES/EXPORT plan-gate actually wired end-to-end?
questions.a: YES — PlanGateInterceptor is registered globally in PlanGateWebConfig; CampaignTemplateControllerTest proves both the 402 (free plan) and 201 (pro plan) cases through the real interceptor, 9/9 green.

questions.q: Does campaign duplicate() reset transient HYPE fields (slotsFilled) so a copy doesn't report phantom filled slots?
questions.a: NO — Campaign.duplicateCopy() copies hypeConfigJson verbatim; slotsFilled carries over. See CAMP-02.

questions.q: Are delete() and duplicate() covered by any test at all?
questions.a: NO — zero references to either method anywhere under influora-api/src/test.

questions.q: Is creator visibility correctly enforced for DRAFT/invite-only campaigns in the creator marketplace?
questions.a: YES — CreatorCampaignService.requireVisibleCampaign filters DRAFT and un-invited private campaigns to a uniform CAMPAIGN_NOT_FOUND 404; backed by 22 passing CreatorCampaignServiceTest cases.

questions.q: Does GET /creators/{creatorId} (CreatorController) ever collide with GET /creators/external/* (ExternalCreatorController)?
questions.a: No functional collision expected — Spring resolves the literal '/creators/external' pattern ahead of the '/creators/{creatorId}' variable pattern by specificity; no test or log evidence of misrouting found, and this is a standard, well-supported Spring MVC pattern.

questions.q: Does the ScoreCalculationJob's schedule and lock match the spec's '0 0 4 UTC'?
Does the report export endpoint serve the correct Content-Type for csv vs pdf?
questions.a: NO — ReportExportController hardcodes application/octet-stream regardless of format, ignoring ExportedFile.contentType(); masked in practice by the FE's <a download> flow, which names the file by extension. See CAMP-04 (P3, low impact).

questions.q: Is there any test coverage exercising ReportExportService directly?
questions.a: NO — no ReportExportServiceTest or ReportExportControllerTest exists anywhere in the RC tree.

questions.q: Does the external-creator connect/lookup flow correctly handle concurrent double-submits?
questions.a: YES on the evidence available — extensive REQUIRES_NEW transaction isolation with documented reasoning, and ExternalCreatorServiceTest (10/10) plus a dedicated ExternalCreatorServiceRaceRollbackIsolationTest (present, not run this session) exist.

questions.q: Are creator applications correctly scoped to the authenticated creator only (no IDOR)?
questions.a: YES — every creator-facing method in this domain resolves identity via CreatorContextService.requireCreatorProfile(principal); none of these routes accept a client-supplied creator id.
PARTIALLY — it loads all of a creator's APPLICATION-source collaborations into memory before sorting/paginating; capped page size (50) but not scan size. Low current risk, noted as CAMP-05 (P3).

questions.q: Is the CreatorApplicationService test suite adequate for the surface it covers?
questions.a: NO — only 2 @Test methods exist for a service with pagination, status filtering, and a separate history endpoint; most of that surface is IMPLEMENTED BUT NOT VERIFIED rather than VERIFIED WORKING.

features.authz: Creator identity always from requireCreatorProfile(principal) — no creator-id param anywhere on these routes; history additionally scopes by findByIdAndCreatorId so a foreign dealId 404s indistinguishably from a nonexistent one (documented Kabir R1 IDOR gate).
features.working_condition: Lists the creator's own applications (never brand invites) sorted by appliedAt desc, with an optional status filter and page/limit pagination (MAX_LIMIT=50); returns the full ordered history timeline for one owned application.
features.failure_conditions: Unknown status filter value 400s (INVALID_STATUS); a foreign or nonexistent dealId on history 404s (DEAL_NOT_FOUND).
features.security_conditions: Same IDOR-closed identity pattern as CreatorCampaignController.
features.tests: CreatorApplicationServiceTest — only 2 @Test methods, ran green this session — thin relative to the service's real surface (pagination boundaries, status filtering, history ordering, and the N+1-avoidance batch-loading of campaigns/workspaces are none of them individually asserted by name). No controller-level test exists for CreatorApplicationController.
features.evidence: Read CreatorApplicationService.java (159 lines) in full. Ran CreatorApplicationServiceTest -> 2/2 green (direct exit code).
known_issues: CAMP-05 (P3): list() loads ALL of a creator's APPLICATION-source collaborations into memory (collaborationRepository.findByCreatorIdAndSource has no Pageable) before sorting and slicing for the page — MAX_LIMIT caps the page size but not the underlying scan.
Only 2 tests for a service with pagination, status filtering, cross-table joins, and a separate history endpoint.
required_fixes: Add tests for status filtering, pagination boundaries, and history ordering/ownership (cross-creator 404 on history).
Consider a Pageable-based repository query if per-creator application volume grows.

features.name: Job: ScoreCalculationJob (0 0 4 UTC)
features.user_type: System (background scheduled job; output consumed by brands via creator discovery)
features.purpose: Compute and persist fake-follower / quality / rate-estimation (and, when enabled, brand-safety) scores for every discoverable creator once daily.
features.classification: VERIFIED WORKING — cron schedule matches the spec's stated '0 0 4 UTC', ShedLock-protected against overlapping runs, real test suite green this session.
features.flow: Spring @Scheduled trigger, @SchedulerLock-protected -> CreatorProfileRepository (discoverable specification) -> per creator: CreatorMetricsRepository + MediaMetricsRepository -> FakeFollowerDetectionService/QualityScoreService/RateEstimationService (+ an optional, capped, rotating BrandSafetyScoreService fan-out) -> CreatorScoreRepository.save (one new time-series row per creator per run) -> read back by CreatorDiscoveryService.loadScoresByCreator and surfaced via GET /creators, /creators/{id}, /creators/featured, /creators/suggestions
features.api: N/A — internal scheduled job, not HTTP-triggered.
features.database: creator_scores (new row per creator per run, never an in-place update — a time series); reads creator_metrics/media_metrics.
features.working_condition: Runs daily at 04:00 UTC, scores every discoverable creator that has at least one metrics snapshot, gracefully skips (logs, does not error) creators with no metrics yet, and optionally brand-safety-scores a capped, staleness-prioritized rotating subset when the feature flag is on.
features.failure_conditions: Per-creator exceptions are caught and logged, never abort the batch (mirrors MetricsPollingJob's resilience pattern); a brand-safety-scoring failure degrades only the 3 brand-safety columns to null on that row, never the fake-follower/quality/rate scores on the same row.
features.tests: ScoreCalculationJobTest — 7 tests, ran green this session, including the documented materialize-then-sort fix for the brand-safety target-selection comparator (an earlier version re-queried the DB O(N log N) times; this was caught and fixed by a Kavya/Kabir QA finding per the class javadoc).
features.production_conditions: Requires the ShedLock table/mechanism to be configured for the distributed lock to work; BrandSafetyScoringProperties.isEnabled() is OFF by default (documented Priya ruling — cost/volume concern), so the 3 brand-safety columns stay null on every row in production until explicitly turned on.
features.evidence: Read ScoreCalculationJob.java (366 lines) in full. Ran ScoreCalculationJobTest -> 7/7 green (direct exit code).
known_issues: Brand-safety scoring is off by default — a real gap versus the full original spec's ambition, but a documented, intentional one guarding against an unbounded per-creator LLM-classification cost, not a bug.

findings.title: CampaignService.create() lets a brand publish a campaign directly to ACTIVE with no funded-escrow check and no publish-fee charge
findings.location: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/CampaignService.java:145-235 (create, no requireFundedEscrow/chargeOnPublish call) vs lines 368-377 (update()'s transitioningToActive branch, which calls both); requireFundedEscrow defined at lines 704-714, called only from update() line 369 and ConfirmLaunchExecutor.java (~line 269/339); CampaignWriteRequest.status is an unrestricted CampaignStatus field (web/dto/campaign/CampaignDtos.java:64). FE trigger sites: src/components/brand/campaigns/campaign-form.tsx:622-663 (handleSubmit, 'Publish' button at line 1695 calls handleSubmit('ACTIVE')) and src/pages/brand-new-hype-campaign.tsx:221-274 (default Launch action, submit('ACTIVE') -> api.campaigns.create).
findings.evidence: Full read of CampaignService.create() (lines 145-235) shows no call to requireFundedEscrow() or brandCampaignFeeService.chargeOnPublish() anywhere in the method, regardless of the incoming status. A repo-wide grep for both symbols returns exactly 2 call sites each, both inside update() and ConfirmLaunchExecutor's Meera confirm_launch tool — create() appears in neither. CampaignWriteRequest.status carries no bean-validation restriction, so a POST /campaigns body can set status=ACTIVE directly. CampaignActivationGatesTest (3/3 green this session) exercises ONLY the update()->ACTIVE path; there is no equivalent test for create()->ACTIVE. Both real product UI entry points (campaign-form.tsx's Publish button and brand-new-hype-campaign.tsx's default Launch submit) call api.campaigns.create with status:'ACTIVE' directly, not create-then-PATCH.
findings.impact: A brand can publish a campaign (standard OR HYPE) straight to ACTIVE via the real 'Publish'/'Launch' UI — making it immediately visible and applicable to creators (CampaignSpecs.browsableForCreator only checks status==ACTIVE && !isPrivate) — while never funding an EscrowHold and never being charged the brand publish fee that BrandCampaignFeeService.chargeOnPublish exists to collect. This is a direct revenue-loss and escrow-policy-bypass path through the domain's primary, everyday create flow, not a hypothetical crafted-request edge case.
findings.recommended_fix: In CampaignService.create(), when the resolved status is ACTIVE, run the identical requireFundedEscrow(campaign.getId()) + brandCampaignFeeService.chargeOnPublish(campaign, workspace.getId()) sequence update() runs at its transitioningToActive edge (after save, inside the same @Transactional boundary) — or, simpler and safer, reject POST /campaigns with status=ACTIVE outright (400/409) and require every campaign to go through create-as-DRAFT-then-PATCH-to-ACTIVE, which is the only path that is actually gated today.
findings.verification_required: Runtime: as a verified brand with zero EscrowHold rows and a Free-or-Pro plan, POST /campaigns with a valid body and status:'ACTIVE'; confirm the response is 201 with the campaign ACTIVE, that no EscrowHold row exists for it, that no WalletTransaction publish-fee debit was recorded, and that it now appears in GET /creator/campaigns (browsableForCreator).

findings.title: Campaign.duplicateCopy() inherits the source's HYPE slotsFilled instead of resetting it for the new DRAFT copy
findings.location: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/domain/entity/Campaign.java:477-506 (duplicateCopy, .hypeConfigJson(hypeConfigJson) at line 501, copying the source's raw JSON unchanged); consumed by influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/admin/AdminCampaignService.java:120-129 (hypeOps aggregates filledSlots += cfg.path("slotsFilled").asInt(0) across ACTIVE HYPE campaigns).
findings.evidence: duplicateCopy() copies hypeConfigJson byte-for-byte from the source campaign and never re-parses/resets it, unlike CampaignService.normalizeHype() (lines 462-479) which explicitly defaults slotsFilled to 0 on a fresh create. Zero tests reference duplicate() anywhere in the test tree, so this was never asserted either way.
findings.impact: A brand duplicates a HYPE campaign that already has filled slots, then republishes the copy (a fresh DRAFT with zero real collaborators) — the copy's stored hype config still reports the OLD slotsFilled count, which AdminCampaignService.hypeOps sums into the platform's avgFillRate ops metric, corrupting that operational dashboard number. Not user-facing or financial, but a real, reproducible data-integrity bug.
findings.recommended_fix: In Campaign.duplicateCopy(), parse the source's hypeConfigJson and reset slotsFilled (and any other run-derived field such as liveUntil) to the same fresh-campaign defaults CampaignService.normalizeHype() applies on create, before persisting the copy.
findings.verification_required: Unit test: build a HYPE campaign with hypeConfigJson containing slotsFilled>0, call duplicateCopy(), assert the returned copy's hypeConfigJson has slotsFilled=0.

findings.title: Five of this domain's public controllers have zero controller-level (HTTP-binding) test coverage
findings.location: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/web/CampaignController.java, CreatorController.java, ExternalCreatorController.java, ReportExportController.java, CreatorApplicationController.java — no corresponding file under influora-api/src/test/java/com/influora/web/
findings.evidence: An exhaustive filename search of influora-api/src/test/java/com/influora/web for CampaignController*, CreatorController*, ExternalCreatorController*, ReportExportController*, CreatorApplicationController* returns nothing. Only CampaignTemplateControllerTest.java and CreatorCampaignControllerTest.java exist for this domain's 7 controllers (both ran green this session: 9/9 and 3/3). The corresponding SERVICE layer for these 5 controllers is well-tested and all ran green this session (CampaignServiceTest 35/35, CreatorDiscoveryServiceTest 27/27, ExternalCreatorServiceTest 10/10, CreatorApplicationServiceTest 2/2) — the gap is specifically at the HTTP-binding/security-filter-chain layer.
findings.impact: Controller-layer regressions — a wrong HTTP verb/path binding, a broken @Valid annotation, a misconfigured Spring Security rule, an ApiResponse JSON envelope shape drift — would not be caught by CI for 30 of this domain's endpoints; only unit-level service logic is protected by the existing tests.
findings.recommended_fix: Add MockMvc-based controller tests for CampaignController, CreatorController, ExternalCreatorController, ReportExportController, and CreatorApplicationController, mirroring the existing CampaignTemplateControllerTest/CreatorCampaignControllerTest pattern — including the still-untested 402 plan-gate case for ReportExportController.
findings.verification_required: N/A — this is an absence-of-coverage finding, confirmed by exhaustive repository search rather than runtime reproduction.

findings.title: ReportExportController always serves Content-Type: application/octet-stream regardless of format=csv|pdf
findings.location: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/web/ReportExportController.java:46-51 (hardcoded MediaType.APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM); influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/ReportExportService.java:118,124 (ExportedFile.contentType populated correctly as text/csv / application/pdf but never read by the controller).
findings.evidence: ExportedFile is a record with a real contentType field, correctly set by renderCsv/renderPdf, but ReportExportController.export() ignores file.contentType() entirely and always sets APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM. Verified the FE consumer (src/pages/brand-campaign-detail.tsx:604-629) downloads via URL.createObjectURL(blob) plus a hidden <a download="campaign-{id}-report.{format}"> element, whose download attribute forces the correct filename/extension client-side regardless of the Blob's MIME type — so the browser still saves a correctly named/typed file in the one real consumer this repo has today.
findings.impact: Low in the current codebase — no observed functional break given the existing FE download path — but any other consumer that inspects the Content-Type header (a programmatic fetch caller, an email-attachment pipeline, a future non-anchor-download client) would see the wrong MIME type.
findings.recommended_fix: Set the response Content-Type from file.contentType() instead of hardcoding APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM.
findings.verification_required: curl -I against GET /campaigns/{id}/export?format=pdf as an authenticated Pro-plan brand and inspect the Content-Type response header.

findings.title: CreatorApplicationService.list() loads a creator's entire APPLICATION-source collaboration history into memory before sorting and paginating
findings.location: influora-api/src/main/java/com/influora/service/CreatorApplicationService.java:75-96 (collaborationRepository.findByCreatorIdAndSource has no Pageable parameter; the full result is materialized, then .stream().sorted(...).toList() and List.subList() slice the requested page).
findings.evidence: collaborationRepository.findByCreatorIdAndSource(creatorUserId, CollaborationSource.APPLICATION) returns a plain List with no page/limit pushed to the database; MAX_LIMIT=50 caps the RESPONSE page size but not the underlying scan size, which grows unbounded with a creator's total application count.
findings.impact: Not a correctness bug today, and no test or production signal indicates this is currently a problem — but a creator with a very large application history would pay an O(n) DB fetch plus an in-memory sort on every single page load of 'My Applications', a scale concern worth addressing before it becomes user-visible latency.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a Pageable-based repository query (e.g. findByCreatorIdAndSourceOrderByAppliedAtDesc(creatorId, source, Pageable)) once per-creator application volume becomes a real concern; not urgent at current scale.
findings.verification_required: Would need a load test against a creator holding several thousand application rows to observe measurable latency; not reproducible from static analysis alone.
